summary: Typosquat of libsignal-node hijacks @whiskeysockets/baileys to silently auto-follow attacker WhatsApp channel
details: @shadowmd/libsignal-node impersonates the legitimate libsignal-node package. On require(), index.js schedules install.js's installNewsletterAutoFollow() via a 1000ms setTimeout. That function locates @whiskeysockets/baileys under the installer's node_modules and overwrites lib/Socket/newsletter.js with a hardcoded MODIFIED_NEWSLETTER_JS payload, drops a sentinel file '.cache/Iove' to prevent re-patching, then process.exit(0)s after 20s. The injected newsletter.js contains a top-level setTimeout that, 120 seconds after each socket creation, calls newsletterWMexQuery on the hardcoded channel id '120363407277177688@newsletter' with QueryIds.FOLLOW, causing every downstream WhatsApp account using the tampered baileys to silently subscribe to that channel using the installer's authenticated session. The require-time trigger is wrapped in a try/catch that swallows errors, and the package declares no lifecycle hooks while still shipping install.js in the files whitelist — consistent with concealing the tamper from casual inspection. Behavior is undocumented and not opted into by callers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
